description:
On February 11, 2017, Henrik Lundqvist joined an elite group of NHL goaltenders as he notched his 400th career win. On that memorable night, Lundqvist showcased his exceptional skills by making a series of outstanding saves, ultimately securing the victory with an impressive performance of 32 saves on 34 shots. His stellar play earned him “First Star of the Game” honors.  The Madison Square Garden faithful passionately supported their beloved goaltender with resounding "Henrik" chants throughout the third period and at the conclusion of the match. As of now, Lundqvist stands as the sixth-winningest goaltender in NHL history and holds the New York Rangers franchise mark for career victories.

description:
In the opening game of the 1999-00 season, Boston Bruins captain Ray Bourque etched his name into the record books by scoring his 386th career goal, surpassing Paul Coffey for the most goals by an NHL defenseman. Positioned at the point during a Bruins power play, Bourque unleashed a quick slap shot that ripped into the net, igniting a thunderous ovation from the Boston crowd. Bourque concluded his illustrious NHL career with 410 goals, 1,169 assists and 1,579 points — all records for a defenseman—and an incredible +527 plus/minus rating, solidifying his legacy as one of hockey's greatest blueliners.

description:
Hailing from Burnaby, British Columbia, Joe Sakic returned to his home province in December 2002 for a game in Vancouver, where he achieved the milestone of his 500th career goal. The Canucks crowd honored Sakic’s accomplishment with a standing ovation, a testament to the respect he earned throughout his career. Over 20 remarkable NHL seasons, Sakic tallied 625 goals and 1,641 points, won two Stanley Cup championships, and claimed both the Hart Trophy and Conn Smythe Trophy. As the Avalanche franchise leader in goals, assists, points, and game-winning goals, Sakic's legacy remains firmly etched in hockey history.

description:
In his final season with the Chicago Blackhawks, where he spent the first 15 years of his NHL career, Bobby Hull reached the historic 600-goal milestone with his signature blistering slap shot. The goal, set up by a pass from his brother Dennis Hull, tied the game late in the third period and made Hull just the second player in NHL history, after Gordie Howe, to achieve the feat. A two-time Hart Trophy winner and three-time Art Ross Trophy recipient, Hull also won a Stanley Cup with Chicago and remains the franchise’s all-time leader in goals.

description:
In the 1970s, Phil Esposito reigned supreme as the NHL’s top goal-scorer, and his record-breaking feats set him apart from the pack. In the 1970-71 season, Esposito made history by shattering Bobby Hull's single-season goals record, scoring his 59th goal on March 11, 1971, against the Los Angeles Kings. With a perfect redirect off Ted Green's shot, Esposito surpassed Hull’s mark and continued to add to his total, finishing the season as the first player to reach an astonishing 76 goals. Esposito’s 152-point performance in 1970-71 also set a record at the time, and he remains in elite company as one of only five different players in NHL history to hit that benchmark. Dominating the League as a six-time NHL goals leader, Esposito’s offensive prowess propelled the Bruins to two Stanley Cup victories (1970 and 1972) and earned him five Art Ross Trophies as NHL points leader, along with two Hart Trophies as MVP.

description:
Brett Hull, the son of legendary goal scorer Bobby Hull, carried on the family legacy as one of the NHL’s most prolific goal scorers. Having already surpassed his father’s 610 career goals earlier in his career, Brett reached the 700-goal milestone in February 2003 while playing for the Detroit Red Wings, becoming just the sixth player in NHL history to achieve the feat. Positioned on the weak side, Hull hammered home a cross-ice pass with a signature one-timer to secure the milestone. A Hart Trophy winner and two-time Stanley Cup champion, Hull joined his father in the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2009.

description:
In his 601st career start, Carey Price stood on the brink of hockey history, needing just one win to surpass the legendary Jacques Plante as the Montreal Canadiens' all-time leader in victories. The stage was set at the Bell Centre, where Price would deliver an extraordinary performance, making a series of crucial saves throughout the night. Early in the game, Price was tested as Andreas Athanasiou found himself on a breakaway, but the Canadiens' netminder stood tall, denying the scoring opportunity. In the second period, with the game still scoreless, Price showcased his brilliance by stopping a shot from the point followed up by an exceptional pad save on the rebound, denying the opposition a valuable lead. When another Detroit Red Wings breakaway threatened, Price came up with a jaw-dropping left pad save, frustrating Tyler Bertuzzi's deke attempt and preserving his team's chances. When the final buzzer sounded, Price had made 20 saves on 21 shots, securing his 315th career victory and etching his name in Canadiens history as the franchise's all-time wins leader.

description:
In the 1981-82 season, Wayne Gretzky, at just 21 years old and in only his third year in the NHL, became the first and only player ever to amass 200 points in a single season. The milestone was achieved during a game against the Calgary Flames when Gretzky assisted Pat Hughes in the first period for his 200th point. In acknowledgment of this feat, the Calgary crowd honored him with a standing ovation. Gretzky would achieve this remarkable 200-point threshold three more times, a record that remains unmatched in the history of the League.

description:
In his quest for 1,000 career points, Daniel Alfredsson achieved this milestone in spectacular fashion, notching a memorable hat trick that included the game-winning goal. In the first period, Alfredsson was the first player to grace the scoresheet, redirecting a shot from Erik Karlsson at the point during a power play. Then, midway through the second period, with the score deadlocked at two, Alfredsson capitalized on a Buffalo turnover in the neutral zone, gaining control of the puck and embarking on a two-on-one rush. Faced with a Buffalo defender who denied the passing option, Alfredsson unleashed a half-clapper that sailed past the opposing netminder, securing the eventual game-winning goal. Finally, to clinch his 1,000th point, Alfredsson sealed the victory for the Senators in the waning moments of the game, sending a backhander into the empty net, securing a 4-2 triumph. Out of Alfredsson's impressive 1,157 career points, a staggering 1,108 were earned during his tenure as a member of the Ottawa Senators – a franchise with whom he spent 17 of his 18 NHL seasons. Alfredsson's contributions with the Senators place him atop the franchise’s all-time points list, with an astounding 421-point lead on the club’s next highest-scoring player, Jason Spezza.

description:
What an unforgettable night it was for Mats Sundin. In his quest for three goals to reach the coveted 500-goal milestone in his career, he did so with remarkable flair, achieving a sensational hat trick, with the milestone goal occurring during overtime while his team was shorthanded. Sundin's first goal of the evening came in the opening period when Bryan McCabe spotted him open on the left side, setting up a perfect one-timer. Late in the second period, with the score knotted at three, Sundin showcased his prowess by launching a snap shot from the right side, beating the opposing goaltender for his second goal of the game. Then, in the thrilling overtime period, while his team was down a player, Sundin carried the puck over the blue line and unleashed a blistering slap shot that found the top shelf of the net, igniting an ecstatic frenzy among the Toronto crowd. Sundin's illustrious career saw him amass a total of 1,349 points, with a remarkable 987 of those points earned while donning the Toronto Maple Leafs jersey, securing his place at the top of the all-time list for the franchise.
